## Write the depreciation formula
Depreciation of 15% each year multiplies the value by $1 - 0.15 = 0.85$ each year, for 5 years.
A &= 30000(1 - 0.15)^5
&= 30000(0.85)^5
## Work out the power
(0.85)^5 &= 0.4437053125
## Multiply by 30 000
A &= 30000 \times 0.4437053125
&= 13311.159375
&\approx \text{€}13311.16
ANSWER: \text{€}13311.16

## Write the compound interest formula
Let $P$ be the sum invested. After 2 years at 3% it is worth $P(1 + 0.03)^2$.
P(1 + 0.03)^2 &= 30000
P(1.03)^2 &= 30000
## Divide both sides by $1.03^2$
P &= \frac{30000}{1.03^2}
## Evaluate
1.03^2 &= 1.0609
## Divide
P &= \frac{30000}{1.0609}
&\approx \text{€}28277.88
ANSWER: \text{€}28277.88

## Write the compound interest formula
Let $r$ be the yearly rate as a decimal. After 3 years, €25 000 grows to $25000(1 + r)^3$.
25000(1 + r)^3 &= 26530.2
## Divide both sides by 25 000
(1 + r)^3 &= \frac{26530.2}{25000}
&= 1.061208
## Take the cube root of both sides
1 + r &= \sqrt[3]{1.061208}
&= 1.02
## Subtract 1 and convert to a percentage
r &= 0.02
&= 2\%
ANSWER: r = 2\%

## Read the point $z_1$ off the diagram
$z_1 = a + bi$ is at $(a, b)$: $a$ is across (real axis) and $b$ is up or down (imaginary axis).
The point is 3 across and 1 down, so $a = 3$ and $b = -1$.
ANSWER: a = 3, \; b = -1

## Write $z_2$ as a point
$z_2 = -1 + 2i$ has real part $-1$ and imaginary part $2$, so it is the point $(-1, 2)$.
## Plot it
Go 1 unit left of the origin along the real axis, then 2 units up. Mark the point and label it $z_2$.
ANSWER: z_2 \text{ plotted at } (-1, 2)

## Substitute $z_1$ and $z_2$
z_3 &= \frac{z_1}{z_2}
&= \frac{3 - i}{-1 + 2i}
## Multiply top and bottom by the conjugate of the denominator
The conjugate of $-1 + 2i$ is $-1 - 2i$.
z_3 &= \frac{(3 - i)(-1 - 2i)}{(-1 + 2i)(-1 - 2i)}
## Expand the numerator
(3 - i)(-1 - 2i) &= -3 - 6i + i + 2i^2
&= -3 - 5i + 2i^2
Use $i^2 = -1$.
&= -3 - 5i - 2
&= -5 - 5i
## Expand the denominator
(-1 + 2i)(-1 - 2i) &= 1 - 4i^2
&= 1 + 4
&= 5
## Divide
z_3 &= \frac{-5 - 5i}{5}
&= -1 - i
ANSWER: z_3 = -1 - i

## Expand the left-hand bracket
2z - 6(4 - 6i) &= (-1 + i)(4 - 2i)
2z - 24 + 36i &= (-1 + i)(4 - 2i)
## Expand the right-hand side
(-1 + i)(4 - 2i) &= -4 + 2i + 4i - 2i^2
Use $i^2 = -1$.
&= -4 + 6i + 2
&= -2 + 6i
## Solve for $z$
2z - 24 + 36i &= -2 + 6i
2z &= 22 - 30i
z &= 11 - 15i
ANSWER: z = 11 - 15i

## Differentiate
f(x) &= 3x^2 - 6x - 8
f'(x) &= 6x - 6
## Set the derivative to zero
At a turning point the slope is zero.
6x - 6 &= 0
6x &= 6
x &= 1
## Find the $y$-value
f(1) &= 3(1)^2 - 6(1) - 8
&= 3 - 6 - 8
&= -11
## Check it is a minimum
The $x^2$ coefficient is positive, so the curve is U-shaped and the turning point is a minimum.
ANSWER: (1, -11)

## Expand the brackets
11x - 5(2x - 1) &= 3(6 - x) + 3
11x - 10x + 5 &= 3(6 - x) + 3
11x - 10x + 5 &= 18 - 3x + 3
## Collect like terms
x + 5 &= 21 - 3x
## Get the $x$ terms on one side
4x + 5 &= 21
## Solve
4x &= 16
x &= 4
ANSWER: x = 4

## Isolate $y$ in the linear equation
y + 5 &= 2x
y &= 2x - 5
## Substitute into the quadratic
x^2 + y^2 &= 25
x^2 + (2x - 5)^2 &= 25
## Expand the bracket
$(2x - 5)^2 = (2x - 5)(2x - 5) = 4x^2 - 20x + 25$.
x^2 + 4x^2 - 20x + 25 &= 25
5x^2 - 20x + 25 &= 25
5x^2 - 20x &= 0
## Factorise and solve for $x$
5x(x - 4) &= 0
x = 0 \quad &\text{or} \quad x = 4
## Find $y$ for each $x$ using $y = 2x - 5$
x = 0: \quad y &= 2(0) - 5 = -5
x = 4: \quad y &= 2(4) - 5 = 3
ANSWER: (x, y) = (0, -5) \text{ or } (4, 3)

## Write the Trapezoidal rule
$A = \frac{h}{2}\left[\text{first} + \text{last} + 2(\text{sum of the others})\right]$, with $h = 3$.
First height $= 4$, last height $= 8$. The others are 5.8, 7, 6.5, 6, 4.8, 6, 6.5.
## Substitute
A &= \frac{3}{2}\left[4 + 8 + 2(5.8 + 7 + 6.5 + 6 + 4.8 + 6 + 6.5)\right]
## Add the middle heights
A &= \frac{3}{2}\left[4 + 8 + 2(42.6)\right]
## Multiply out
A &= \frac{3}{2}\left[12 + 85.2\right]
&= \frac{3}{2}(97.2)
&= 145.8 \text{ m}^2
ANSWER: 145.8 \text{ m}^2

## Write the Trapezoidal rule
Now $h = 4$. First height $= 4$, last height $= 8$. The others are 6.4, 6.9, 6, $x$, 6.2.
## Substitute
145.6 &= \frac{4}{2}\left[4 + 8 + 2(6.4 + 6.9 + 6 + x + 6.2)\right]
## Simplify inside the brackets
145.6 &= 2\left[12 + 2(25.5 + x)\right]
145.6 &= 2\left[12 + 51 + 2x\right]
145.6 &= 2(63 + 2x)
145.6 &= 126 + 4x
## Solve for $x$
4x &= 19.6
x &= 4.9
ANSWER: x = 4.9 \text{ m}

## Find the commission on the first 1000 of sales
\text{Commission} &= 20\% \times 1000
&= 0.2 \times 1000
&= \text{€}200
## Find the sales above 1000
3000 - 1000 &= 2000
## Find the commission at 30% on those sales
\text{Commission} &= 30\% \times 2000
&= 0.3 \times 2000
&= \text{€}600
## Add the basic salary and both commissions
\text{Income} &= 150 + 200 + 600
&= \text{€}950
ANSWER: \text{€}950

## Take away the basic salary and the first commission
Basic salary plus the commission on the first $\text{€}1000$ is $\text{€}350$, and $\text{€}1160$ is more than this, so some sales were above $\text{€}1000$.
1160 - 150 - 200 &= 810
&= \text{€}810
## The remaining 810 is 30% of the sales above 1000
0.3x &= 810
x &= \frac{810}{0.3}
x &= 2700
## Add the first 1000 of sales
\text{Total sales} &= 1000 + 2700
&= \text{€}3700
ANSWER: \text{€}3700

## Spot how each pattern grows
Pattern $n$ has a top row of $n+2$ tiles and a leg of $n$ tiles hanging below each end.
Pattern 3 has 5 on top and legs of 3, so pattern 4 has 6 on top and legs of 4.
## Draw pattern 4
Add one tile to the top row and one tile to the bottom of each leg. The new pattern is drawn in blue.
ANSWER: \text{Pattern 4: top row of 6 tiles, a leg of 4 tiles at each end}

## Count the tiles in each pattern
\text{Pattern 1} &= 3 + 1 + 1 = 5
\text{Pattern 2} &= 4 + 2 + 2 = 8
\text{Pattern 3} &= 5 + 3 + 3 = 11
\text{Pattern 4} &= 6 + 4 + 4 = 14
## Each pattern has 3 more tiles than the one before
\text{Pattern 5} &= 14 + 3 = 17
## Complete the table
$n=1$: 5 tiles, $n=2$: 8, $n=3$: 11, $n=4$: 14, $n=5$: 17.
ANSWER: 5,\ 8,\ 11,\ 14,\ 17

## Find the first term and the common difference
The tile numbers $5, 8, 11, \dots$ go up by the same amount each time, so the pattern is arithmetic.
a &= 5
d &= 8 - 5 = 3
d &= 3
## Substitute into the formula for the nth term
T_n &= a + (n-1)d
T_n &= 5 + (n-1)3
&= 5 + 3n - 3
&= 3n + 2
## Read off p and q
Compare $3n+2$ with $pn+q$.
p &= 3
q &= 2
ANSWER: p = 3,\ q = 2

## Substitute n = 20 into T_n = 3n + 2
T_{20} &= 3(20) + 2
&= 60 + 2
&= 62
ANSWER: 62\text{ tiles}

## Set T_n equal to 290
3n + 2 &= 290
3n &= 290 - 2
3n &= 288
n &= \frac{288}{3}
n &= 96
ANSWER: \text{Pattern } 96

## Write the formula for the sum of n terms of an arithmetic sequence
The total number of tiles in the first $n$ patterns is the sum of the first $n$ terms, with $a = 5$ and $d = 3$.
S_n &= \frac{n}{2}\left(2a + (n-1)d\right)
## Substitute a = 5 and d = 3
S_n &= \frac{n}{2}\left(2(5) + (n-1)3\right)
&= \frac{n}{2}\left(10 + (n-1)3\right)
## Multiply out the bracket inside
&= \frac{n}{2}\left(10 + 3n - 3\right)
&= \frac{n}{2}\left(3n + 7\right)
## Multiply out the final bracket
&= \frac{n(3n + 7)}{2}
&= \frac{3n^2 + 7n}{2}
ANSWER: S_n = \frac{3n^2 + 7n}{2}

## Plot the six points from the table
Plot $(50, 9250)$, $(60, 10\,900)$, $(70, 12\,350)$, $(80, 13\,600)$, $(90, 14\,650)$ and $(100, 15\,500)$.
## Join the points with a smooth curve
The profit function is a quadratic, so the graph curves gently upwards and flattens as it nears its maximum.
ANSWER: \text{Smooth curve through the six plotted points}

## Draw lines across from 10 000 and 14 000
Draw a horizontal line from $10\,000$ on the profit axis to the curve, and another from $14\,000$.
## Read the values off the x-axis
Drop a vertical line from each meeting point to the $x$-axis and read the values.
Lower value $\approx 54$ km and upper value $\approx 84$ km.
The marking scheme gives 55 and 83; any reading close to the curve is accepted.
ANSWER: \text{Lower} \approx 54\text{ km},\ \text{Upper} \approx 84\text{ km}

## Differentiate the profit function
P(x) &= 275x - x^2 - 2000
P'(x) &= 275 - 2x
## Set the rate of change equal to 105
275 - 2x &= 105
-2x &= 105 - 275
-2x &= -170
x &= \frac{-170}{-2}
x &= 85
ANSWER: x = 85\text{ km}

## Estimate his height using m(x)
m(44.2) &= 2.3(44.2) + 65.53
&= 101.66 + 65.53
&= 167.19
## Find the error
\text{Error} &= 171 - 167.19
&= 3.81
## Write the error as a percentage of the actual height
\text{Percentage error} &= \frac{3.81}{171} \times 100
&= 2.228\ldots\%
&\approx 2.23\%
ANSWER: 2.23\%

## Set the male and female heights equal
2.3x + 65.53 &= 2.5x + 54.13
## Collect the x terms on one side
65.53 - 54.13 &= 2.5x - 2.3x
11.4 &= 0.2x
x &= \frac{11.4}{0.2}
x &= 57
## Find the height by putting x = 57 into m(x)
m(57) &= 2.3(57) + 65.53
&= 131.1 + 65.53
&= 196.63
ANSWER: \text{Femur} = 57\text{ cm},\ \text{Height} = 196.63\text{ cm}

## Subtract the girls from the total births
\text{Boys} &= 65909 - 32290
&= 33619
ANSWER: 33619

## Write the probability as a fraction
$P(\text{boy}) = \dfrac{\text{number of boys}}{\text{total births}}$.
P(\text{boy}) &= \frac{33619}{65909}
## Divide and round to 2 decimal places
&= 0.5101\ldots
&\approx 0.51
ANSWER: 0.51

## Find the probability of a boy and of a girl
Each birth is independent, and $P(\text{boy}) = 0.51$.
P(\text{girl}) &= 1 - 0.51
&= 0.49
## (i) Three boys in a row: multiply
P(\text{B, B, B}) &= 0.51 \times 0.51 \times 0.51
&= 0.132651
&\approx 0.1327
## (ii) Two boys, then a girl: multiply
P(\text{B, B, G}) &= 0.51 \times 0.51 \times 0.49
&= 0.127449
&\approx 0.1274
ANSWER: \text{(i) } 0.1327 \qquad \text{(ii) } 0.1274

## Add the probabilities that are given
\text{Sum} &= 0.14 + 0.15 + 0.18 + 0.15 + 0.12 + 0.1
&= 0.84
## All the probabilities add up to 1
P(\text{Tue}) &= 1 - 0.84
&= 0.16
ANSWER: 0.16

## Multiply the number of babies by P(Tuesday)
\text{Expected} &= 1300 \times 0.16
&= 208
ANSWER: 208
